messages:
maya: quick heads-up — hitting duplicate tool calls in the python sample app when the token refresh happens during an async tool_call. not sure if this is expected behavior or a bug.

maya: minimal snippet below (very small repro):

maya: ```py
from dataclasses import dataclass
from redwood import AsyncClient

client = AsyncClient(api_key=\"...\")

@dataclass
class Person:
    name: str
    age: int

# this sometimes causes the tool to be invoked twice when token refresh kicks in
res = await client.tool_call(
    \"lookup_person\",
    input={\"id\": \"123\"},
    output_type=Person,
)
print(res)
```

maya: logs show duplicate invocation:

maya: ```
INFO request_id=abc123 send to tool lookup_person
WARNING token refresh started
INFO request_id=abc123 retrying request
INFO tool invoked: lookup_person args={\"id\":\"123\"}
INFO tool invoked: lookup_person args={\"id\":\"123\"}  # duplicate
```

maya: any ideas? should we be adding idempotency keys on tool calls?

dan: this sounds like the client auto-retry re-sends the same outgoing RPC while the token refresh was in-flight. if the underlying transport doesn't dedupe, you'll hit the tool twice.

dan: quick workaround: disable auto_retry or add a custom request_id header and dedupe on the tool side.

maya: @dan where do we pass request_id? i don't see a param on AsyncClient.tool_call right now.

priya: fwiw i've also seen the structured output coercion be flaky — if tool returns a json-string instead of object, dataclass conversion blows up. we should support some coercion flags and a strict mode.

priya: proposal: let tool_call accept coerce_output=True and idempotency_key optional. sdk would attach X-Request-Id and X-Idempotency-Key headers.

alex: good catches. this is a bug — token refresh path shouldn't cause duplicate downstream calls. i'll file an issue and add a test matrix for token-refresh + retry + async toolcall.

maya: thanks. repro is in my fork: https://github.com/redwood/repro-samples/tree/maya/async-toolcall-retry (small README in root)

dan: for an immediate patch i can add a non-retrying transport wrapper around the tool_call RPC (so token refresh is done before the attempt). probably a stopgap.

alex: please do that as a draft PR and link the issue. also add a unit test that asserts exactly one invocation of the tool when refresh triggers (use monkeypatch on the transport).

ci-bot: created issue redwood/sdk#3421 — \"async tool_call duplicates on token refresh + retry\" (assigned to @alex). https://github.com/redwood/sdk/issues/3421

maya: adding one more ask — can we expose the SDK-generated request_id in the ToolCallResponse so apps can correlate logs? currently it's only in client debug logs.

alex: agreed. i'll extend the response object to include request_id and include an opt-in header injection for idempotency_key. will also surface a coerce_output flag for dataclass coercion and a strict_validation mode.

priya: for the dataclass path, can we add an optional hook like on_parse_failure that returns fallback value instead of raising? helps for noisy external tools.

alex: yup — that sounds useful for sample apps. i'll sketch API: tool_call(..., coerce_output=False, strict=False, on_parse_failure=None, idempotency_key=None)

maya: perfect. i'll add a regression sample to repro-samples and link to the issue. thx! :thumbsup:

dan: will follow up with a small transport wrapper PR.

ci-bot: linked PR redwood/sdk#5428 to issue #3421

maya: leaving logs and minimal repro steps in the issue, ping me if you need access to the private tool endpoint.
